title: A gas-free graphite outflow fits the infrared excess of Gaia20cdd and gives a short 4.6 um dust response
abstract: We test whether escaping grains can make the reported infrared excess of Gaia20cdd. We couple Mie grain heating to exact radiation-pressure trajectories from circular parent orbits. Under direct heating with no gas or collisions, a constant graphite supply fits the two infrared excess measurements. For two size bounds and two host models, best release radii are 2.1-3.4 au, about one-third below static-ring radii. At those best fits, 90 percent of the 4.6 um dust light comes from grains younger than 0.55-0.73 years. The supply is about 2.0-2.7 times 10^22 g per year. An eight-year source orbit remains allowed, but the same escaping grains cannot return. We give response kernels and a test for infrared fading after production stops. The result is conditional: infrared epochs differ, only two excess bands are fitted, and shielding, gas, collisions and a joint optical fit are absent.
